The post raises `invoiced_quantity` and advances the order **INVOICED** (fully invoiced) / **CLOSED** (fully delivered AND invoiced). The finance AR invoice claims its OWN `INV-` number — two numbers, the sales billing triggers the finance doc (mirroring match→bill). **(B) Returns / RMA.** `SalesReturn`/`SalesReturnLine` (`sales_returns`/`_lines`, `DocumentMixin` + gapless `RMA-` number) — a delivery run backwards. Built DRAFT against a delivered+invoiced order (receiving `bin_id` + priced fields snapshot per line); each returned qty ≤ **invoiced − returned** (over-return → 422 `sales.over_return`). **The cap is INVOICED, not delivered:** a credit note must reduce a real invoice, so the customer cannot be credited for more than was invoiced — tracked by a new `returned_quantity` column on `sales_order_lines`. **Post → TWO atomic event-bus legs:** `ReturnReceived` → inventory's handler creates a stock **RECEIPT** move per line with `valuation_offset_account_id` = the item-category **COGS** account (the override, mirroring 6.3's GR/IR override) so the costing posts **Dr Inventory / Cr COGS** — reversing the issue (goods re-enter at current book cost); `ReturnCredited` → finance's handler posts an AR **credit note** **Dr sales-revenue / Cr AR control + reverse output tax** — reversing the billing. **(C) Credit notes in finance: added (4.6 had none).** Finance shipped no credit-note path, so 7.4 adds `finance/service/credit_notes.create_and_post_customer_credit_note`: a credit note is a `CustomerInvoice` row (no new model) whose POSTED journal carries `document_type` **AR_CREDIT_NOTE** and the SIGN-FLIPPED directions of an invoice; it claims a `CN-` number and `open_amount`=0 (a reduction, not an open receivable to dun). The draft build (tax+totals) is shared verbatim via the extracted `create_ar_document_draft` builder — the only differences are the doc type + journal direction. The journal one-side CHECK requires positive amounts, so a credit note posts the reversal on the *flipped* sides (positive), NOT negative amounts. **(D) The order-to-cash GL:** delivery posts Dr COGS / Cr Inventory; billing posts Dr AR / Cr Revenue (+ tax); a full return reverses BOTH — inventory back UP, COGS back DOWN, revenue back DOWN, AR back DOWN — so the AR/revenue/COGS accounts **net to zero** (proven via the finance account-balance projection, the 6.4 GR/IR-clears-to-zero mirror); inventory holds the returned goods' value (they are physically back in stock). **(E) Migration `0031_sales_billing_returns`** (down_revision 0030): four tables + (tenant,status)/(tenant,sales_order_id) indexes + the `returned_quantity` batch-alter column on `sales_order_lines`; NO trigger-bearing alters, reversible, portable both engines, ≤63-char ids, zero autogenerate drift on SQLite + PG. **(F) Structure:** `constants.py`→`constants/` package (enums/permissions/documents, split at the cap, re-exported); `models/billing.py`+`returns.py`, `schemas/billing.py`+`returns.py`, `events.py` (adds `BillingInvoiced`/`ReturnReceived`/`ReturnCredited`); `service/` adds `billing.py`+`billing_post.py`+`billing_reads.py` and `returns.py`+`returns_post.py`+`returns_reads.py`; `router.py` mounts sibling `billing_router.py`+`return_router.py`. Deactivating an ACTIVE version → INACTIVE (kept for history, never deleted). Editing/adding/deleting on a non-DRAFT version → 409. **(c) Multi-level = via references.** The SCHEMA is single-level-per-BOM: a `Bom` header lists DIRECT `BomComponent` lines of one parent. "Multi-level" emerges because a component item can itself be the parent of its OWN `Bom`; the tree is resolved by EXPLOSION at MRP time (8.3), which walks component→its active BOM→its components recursively (visited set + depth cap, the `docflow.get_chain` precedent). The masters reject only a DIRECT self-component (a component whose item IS the BOM's parent — 422 `manufacturing.bom_self_component`); deeper cycles (A→B→A) are an 8.3 explosion-time concern, not expressible on a single-level row. `BomComponent.scrap_percent` is the per-component waste allowance; `Bom.base_quantity` is the parent yield, component `quantity_per` is per base_quantity. **(d) Work centres + routings.** `WorkCenter.capacity_hours_per_day` feeds 8.3's rough capacity check; `efficiency_percent` (default 100) scales throughput; `cost_center_id` is an OPAQUE finance id (D-029, nullable, validated via `finance/queries.cost_center_exists`) for later activity-rate costing. `RoutingOperation` pins a step to a work centre (`work_center_id` is an INTRA-module composite tenant FK) with `setup_time_minutes` (fixed/order) + `run_time_minutes_per_unit` (per unit) — MINUTES as `QuantityType` scale-6 (fractional minutes, exact on both engines, D-015 — never plain Numeric); `operation_number` (10/20/30…) unique per routing, auto-appended as the next multiple of 10. **(e) Opaque cross-module ids + the new `inventory/queries.uom_exists`.** BOM/routing item ids + the BOM UoM ids are opaque inventory ids (no FK to inv_items/inv_uoms), validated via `inventory/queries.item_exists` and a NEW `inventory/queries.uom_exists` (the UoM analogue of `item_exists` — a UoM is a distinct inventory entity, so it could not be folded into `item_exists`; added in 8.1).
